question: Why is Greedy Best-First Search not guaranteed to be optimal or complete?
options: It ignores path cost g(n) and relies only on h(n)
It always chooses the shallowest node
It expands nodes in FIFO order
It requires full knowledge of the goal state in advance
answer: It ignores path cost g(n) and relies only on h(n).
explanation: Greedy search only looks at the heuristic h(n) and ignores the cost g(n) accumulated so far, which can lead it down sub-optimal paths or infinite loops.
